I farm 7.5 mu with just two people in the house, so I will not spread myself too thin. What I know comes from doing it year after year and watching whose field stands thick and whose field goes thin. Around here, wheat-maize is the steady road, so I will keep most of my land in that and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Last year’s way is what I trust first. If I change too much and it fails, the loss is bigger than the money I save. I have well water, so I do not fear drought the same way as dryland people, and I will use that to hold wheat and maize steady. On fertilizer, I would rather put a bit more than come up short. A few extra kilos cost money, but an empty ear or a light boll costs more. So I will keep about 5 mu in wheat-maize and 2.5 mu in cotton. For wheat I will use improved seed like most people around me do now, give it the heavier base manure and three waters if the year is normal. For summer maize I will use hybrid seed, sow right after wheat comes off, mostly no-tillage to save labor, and push nitrogen so the ears fill. Cotton I will keep on the smaller piece because it takes more looking after. I will use improved seed, plough that land clean, give it enough fertilizer for bolls, and spray more times than grain because bugs on cotton do not wait for me.
